quests.title: Tricks
quests.summary: A farm kid in Millbrook with three little tricks and no idea what they mean. Then a stranger in grey walks into the tavern.

stages.description: Ma left a list of chores. Magic makes them quicker. Mostly.

objectives.description: Nudge the spoon off the kitchen table
Light the stove with a finger spark

stages.description: Tam saw the whole thing and is hopping from foot to foot.

objectives.description: Show Tam what you can do

stages.description: Tam wants to see the jar on the fence post jump.

objectives.description: Jolt the jar on the fence post

stages.description: Rook Barlow is picking on Tam by the well again.

objectives.description: Deal with Rook at the well

stages.description: Wolves have been taking sheep from the barley fields at night.

objectives.description: Ask Farmer Hollis about the wolves

stages.description: The wolves are in the barley. Your tricks will have to do.

objectives.description: Drive the wolves out of the barley

stages.description: The barley is quiet. Farmer Hollis will want to know.

objectives.description: Tell Farmer Hollis the wolves are gone

stages.description: Everyone in Millbrook is talking about a stranger at the Mill Wheel.

objectives.description: Go to the Mill Wheel tavern

stages.description: A stranger in a grey cloak sits by the fire, watching you.

objectives.description: Speak to the old man in grey

stages.description: The old man asked you to walk with him up the hill road.

objectives.description: Walk with the old man up the hill road

stages.description: The old man stops at the top of the hill to tell you something.
The old man is gone. All that's left is his hat and a staff that won't stop humming. Go home.
Wardens rode into Millbrook at dawn, asking about the stranger.

objectives.description: Speak to the Wardens in the square

stages.description: The Wardens are gone, for now. The village square is loud with children.

lines.text: The spoon went FLYING. And the stove! Ma says it's the devil's work but Ma also says that about turnips.
Do the jar! The one on the fence post. Make it JUMP.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Stand back.
The jar! On the post! Aim at it and do the zappy one!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The jar leaps off the post in a crackle of blue light and lands in the grass, smoking. Tam claps like it's the King's own fireworks.
One day you'll be a real wizard. Or a mage. Or whatever the other one is. And I'll be your apprentice.

choices.text: You'll be the first to know.
It's just tricks, Tam. Go do your chores.

lines.text: Promise?

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rook Barlow has Tam's cap and is holding it over the well. Tam is trying very hard not to cry.
Oh look, it's the spark freak. Gonna sizzle me? Go on. Try it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Rook dangles the cap over the dark water.

choices.text: Jolt him. Hard.
Give the cap a jolt so it jumps back to Tam.
Tell him you'll fetch the miller. His father.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The jolt cracks like a whip. Rook yelps, drops the cap and sits down hard in the mud. A few people across the square turn to stare.
You're mad. You're actually mad! I'm telling everyone!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A little crack of light and the cap hops out of Rook's hand, right into Tam's. Rook stares at his empty fingers.
That's... how did you... this isn't over, freak.
You wouldn't. ...You would. Fine. Take your stupid cap.

lines.speaker: tam
lines.text: Thanks. You didn't have to. ...But thanks.
Three ewes this week. Three! Something's driving them wolves out of the Fenwood, and into my barley.
Your Ma says you've got a knack for the odd trick. Well, odd's what I need. Wolves don't like a spark in the face.

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: I'll see what I can do.
Mind yourself. They come in threes and they bite.
You did it? Saints. I owe you a pie. Several pies.
Odd thing, though. I looked at one of 'em. Skin and bone. They weren't hunting for sport. Whatever's wrong in the Fenwood, it's starving them.
There'll be more of them. What do you reckon we do?

choices.text: Hunt the rest of the pack before they come back.
Leave scraps at the forest edge. Fed wolves stay away.

lines.text: Hard, but fair. A farm can't feed the forest.
Feeding wolves. Your Ma will say you're soft in the head. ...I'll try it.
Here. My old gloves. Better on your hands than in my drawer.
He's been sat there since noon. Paid in old silver, the kind with the Concord stamp. Asked for you by name, he did.
Go on, then. He doesn't bite. I don't think.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The stranger by the fire wears a long grey cloak and a wide hat, singed at the tip. His staff leans against the chair, humming faintly, like a bee in a jar.
That spoon on the table. Make it move.

choices.text: Nudge the spoon across the table.
Show off: spark, nudge and jolt it all at once.
Who's asking?

lines.text: Someone who walked a very long way to watch a spoon move. Go on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The spoon slides, wobbles and rolls off the edge. Someone at the bar laughs.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The spoon leaps, crackles and spins in the air for a heartbeat before it clatters down, smoking. The bar goes quiet.
Hm. You have more in you than you know.
All three of it.

choices.text: All three of what?
What's your name?

lines.text: The book, the understanding and the fire inside. Most people get one, if they're lucky. You have a little of each, and none of it trained.
Names are heavy things to hand a stranger. Grey will do, for now.
Walk with me. Up the hill road. Some things are better said under the sky.

choices.text: I'll come.
Ma will want me home for supper.

lines.text: Then we'll be quick about it.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He stands, leaning on the worn staff, and nods toward the door.
This is far enough. Listen carefully, because I may not get to say it twice.
This world is held together by a promise older than this hill. That promise is breaking. When it breaks, people like you will matter more than kings.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: He looks up. The sky is perfectly clear.

choices.text: What promise?
People like me? I make spoons move.

lines.text: Today. Today you make spoons move.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sky cracks open.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Light. Noise. A smell like hot iron. When you can see again there is only a scorched hat in the grass, and a worn staff, still humming.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On the ridge, a rider in Warden blue watches you for a long moment. Then turns, and is gone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Your bed. The staff hums quietly where you leaned it against the wall. Tam is already asleep, or pretending to be.

choices.text: Sleep.
Not yet.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You dream of a grey room with no doors. Somewhere far away, a staff is humming.
...can you hear me? The line is thin here. Thinner every day.
Find the Concord.

choices.text: Who are you?
Where are you?
What is the Concord?

lines.text: ...find the Concord... before the promise...

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: You wake to hoofbeats in the lane.
You. You were seen on the hill road yesterday with a vagrant in grey. Where is he now?

lines.speaker: player
lines.text: Lightning hit him. Out of a clear sky. He's... gone.
Gone. Convenient. What did he tell you? What did he give you?

choices.text: Tell them everything, and that you kept his hat and staff.
Tell them about the lightning, but say he left nothing behind.
Say he was talking nonsense and you never saw a thing.

lines.text: A hat and a staff. Hm. Keep them safe and keep them close. Someone will come for them.
Nothing. Struck by lightning and he left nothing, not even a boot. ...If you remember anything, the Wardens will be grateful.
Nonsense, he said? Funny. Half the village says otherwise. Don't leave Millbrook.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The sergeant swings back into the saddle. The Wardens ride out the way they came.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A gang of children is playing Greycloak and the Sundering, the oldest game in the Vale. One of them wears a bucket for a hat.
Stand back, Sundering! I'm the Greycloak, and I'll seal you in a PROMISE!
That's not how it goes! The Greycloak's hat is crooked like a chimney, and his staff SINGS. Yours is a broom.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: On your back, the old man's staff gives a single, quiet hum.
Do the spoon thing again! Please? Just once?
What are you looking at, spark freak?
Barley won't harvest itself. Neither will I, at this rate.
Welcome to the Mill Wheel. Cider's warm, beds are cold, and that's how we like it.
You can't play, you're too old. Unless you can do a REAL spell.
